claim: Let \(T_k=\operatorname{tridiag}(-1,2,-1)\) and define \(D_0(s)=1\), \(D_1(s)=1+2s\), and \(D_j(s)=(1+2s)D_{j-1}(s)-s^2D_{j-2}(s)\). For each \(k\ge 1\), let \(\sigma_k\) be the unique positive solution of \(D_k(\sigma_k)=2D_{k-1}(\sigma_k)\). For the standard Peaceman–Rachford ADI full step for the Dirichlet heat semidiscretization on an \(m\times n\) interior rectangular grid, with \(m,n\ge2\), mesh widths \(h_x,h_y\), and step \(\Delta t\), the one-step matrix is entrywise nonnegative for every nonnegative datum if and only if \(\Delta t/(2h_x^2)\le\sigma_m\) and \(\Delta t/(2h_y^2)\le\sigma_n\). Moreover \(\sigma_1=1/2\), \(\sigma_2=1/\sqrt3\), the sequence is strictly increasing, and \(\sigma_k\uparrow 2-\sqrt2\). Thus on an \(N\times N\) square grid the sharp dimensionless frontier is \(\Delta t/h^2\le2\sigma_N\), tending to \(4-2\sqrt2\). At \(N=2\), \(h=1\), and \(\Delta t=6/5\), the one-dimensional factor is \(\frac1{56}\begin{pmatrix}-1&15\\15&-1\end{pmatrix}\), so the full Peaceman–Rachford matrix has the negative entry \(-15/3136\).
integrity: The finite-grid theorem is proved analytically from exact tridiagonal determinant and inverse identities. Exact rational counterexamples and representative threshold computations are replayable from the included checker. The asymptotic limit is proved analytically rather than inferred from finite experiments.
scientific_limitations: Specific to the standard tensor-product Dirichlet second-difference heat operator and the classical constant-step Peaceman–Rachford factorization; no claim is made for other boundary closures, variable coefficients, nonlinear terms, or modified ADI schemes.
title: Sharp finite-grid positivity threshold for Peaceman–Rachford heat stepping
